title: Cooperative prefetch cancellation and scheduler pruning to reduce tail latency
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem:
We continue to observe >95th and 99th percentile tail latency spikes under mixed workloads caused by long-running inflight prefetches and outdated scheduling paths that serially block short, latency-sensitive requests. The current prefetch implementation aggressively primes KV shards but lacks a cooperative cancellation mechanism, so canceled user requests can leave prefetches running and leaking CPU/GPU slot reservations. The scheduler also contains legacy branching that routes requests through deep reconciliation code paths even when lightweight fast-paths exist.

Impact:
- Visible 99th percentile tail increases during bursty traffic and model changeovers (affects both Hosted and Dedicated).
- Higher unit cost due to wasted compute on stale prefetches and increased queueing.
- Harder to meet latency SLOs for latency-sensitive customers and A/B experiments.

Proposal summary:
1) Implement cooperative cancellation tokens for inflight prefetch and KV priming tasks so they can yield early when the originating request is canceled or superseded.
2) Introduce a lightweight tombstone protocol for inflight prefetch work items to allow safe early reclamation without violating cache invariants.
3) Prune legacy scheduler branches and add a fast-path admission check that short-circuits to low-latency worker lanes for single-shot requests under X tokens.
4) Add observability: per-request prefetch state, cancellation-count metric, and scheduler-path histogram to make regressions visible.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Cooperative cancellation uses a non-blocking atomic flag plus epoch counter to avoid locking the prefetch queue. This avoids high-latency locks but requires careful memory ordering to prevent ABA-like races when reusing work-item structs.
- Tombstone protocol stores a small metadata blob in the KV priming queue instead of a full deletion, enabling idempotent reclamation but adds some minor per-entry overhead.
- Scheduler pruning relies on heuristics about request size and model variant; conservative defaults will ensure we don't prematurely send heavy requests to fast-paths. We will gate changes behind a rollout flag.
- Cost: small memory bump for per-prefetch metadata (~48 bytes per active prefetch) vs expected CPU/GPU savings under load.

Milestones:
- Week 1: Design doc and API sketch, infra metrics added to dashboard (done).
- Week 2: Implement cancellation token and unit tests for work-item lifecycle (in progress).
- Week 3: Implement tombstone reclamation and safety checks, integration tests with KV invariants.
- Week 4: Scheduler fast-path admission with feature flag and e2e load test.
- Week 5: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic, monitor dashboards, iterate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cancellation token successfully cancels >90% of prefetched work within 10ms of request cancel on synthetic tests.
- 99th percentile latency reduces by >=10% on our mixed workload playback in canary.
- No KV cache corruption seen across 1M-request integration run.
- Observability added: prefetched_inflight, prefetch_cancel_count, scheduler_path_histogram.

Test plan:
- Unit tests covering lifecycle of prefetch work item, cancellation racing with completion.
- Property-based tests that simulate reusing work-item structs across epochs to detect ABA.
- Integration test with KV store emulator to validate tombstone semantics under network reorder.
- Load tests: replay 24-hour production trace to compare tail latency and CPU/GPU utilization pre/post change.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag default off in runtime-2.4.
- Step 1: Enable in staging and run replay tests (48h).
- Step 2: Canary 5% for non-enterprise host regions for 72h with automated rollback on any metric regression beyond threshold.
- Step 3: Gradually increase to 25% then 100% with checkpoints.

Metrics and dashboards to watch:
- 95th/99th latency for text.generate and chat.stream routes.
- prefetch_cancel_count (per-region, per-model).
- prefetched_inflight gauge and average-prefetch-duration.
- scheduler_path_histogram to ensure a meaningful shift to fast-paths.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: ABA/memory reuse race introduces subtle correctness bug. Mitigation: epoch counters + load-only QA run; code review by allocator experts.
- Risk: Tombstones increase memory pressure on small nodes. Mitigation: adaptive tombstone GC and fallback to conservative mode on low-memory nodes.
- Risk: Fast-path misclassification could bounce large requests. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and observe before widening.

- Risk: minor bump to nightly test time due to integration work.

Post-deploy follow-ups:
- If the canary shows improvement, open ENG-573211 to extend cooperative cancellation to background prewarmers.
- Add automated alert for rapid rise of prefetched_inflight / prefetch_cancel_count ratio.
